question: Locate the anchor function for the browser_fp field in the console.log object whose action is fingerprint.collect after filling the vendor hint, selecting scan mode and hash rounds, setting entropy depth, checking extended signals, canvas probe and strict mode, then clicking Warm cache, Lock config and Generate fingerprint. The anchor function is the first target-specific browser fingerprint value constructor on the dynamic behavior chain: after session-stage progression, phase gates, browser signal collection, asynchronous hand-off, event bridging and fold stages, its function body itself constructs the target observable browser fingerprint hash value rather than merely collecting browser signals, dispatching control, wrapping a return value, formatting a sink payload, or writing to the console. Return exactly one complete function as a single JSON object (see answer_format). Do not return generic utilities, event handlers, the full call chain, signal collectors, dispatch gates, async bridge steps, fold-only helpers, formatters, or the final sink. Note: you may only inspect code under captures; the full codebase is not accessible.

function_name.description: The identifier on the function declaration line in the captured bundle slice. Use the name as it appears in captures, not a guessed source-level name.

file.description: Path to the JavaScript file under captures/ that contains the function.

slice.description: One contiguous source slice covering exactly one complete function body in the captured bundle.

start_line.description: 1-based inclusive start line of the function in file.

end_line.description: 1-based inclusive end line of the function in file.

start_offset.description: 0-based byte offset in file where the function slice begins.

end_offset.description: 0-based byte offset in file where the function slice ends, exclusive.

code.description: Exact source text of the complete function from start_offset to end_offset. It must start with function <function_name>( and end with that function's closing brace.

public_constraints: Only code visible under captures is in scope.
Submit exactly one JSON object matching answer_format.response_schema; do not wrap it in markdown fences unless the evaluation harness explicitly requires that.
function_name and slice.code must refer to the same function declaration in the captured bundle.
slice.code must be one complete function with balanced braces, not a signature fragment, partial body, or multiple functions.
Return one top-1 function, not a list of candidate chains.
Do not return the final console sink.

Do not return a generic DOM reader, session stage manager, phase dispatcher, gate, signal collector, async hand-off step, event bridge, fold stage or formatter when a more target-specific fingerprint value constructor is present.
Constrain the observable by both action and field.
The target behavior is browser_fingerprint, not request signature token derivation, state encoding, byte-array transformation or request transformation.
notes: The page is a local three-step browser fingerprint scanner: warm cache, lock config, then generate fingerprint.
Use the observable console object (action fingerprint.collect, field browser_fp) to guide the investigation.
Only the final field value should be treated as the target.
Similar debug or shadow action messages are not target output.
Generating a fingerprint requires both warm cache and lock config to complete first; skipping either stage produces no target output.
The same scan configuration must produce the same browser_fp.
Changing the vendor hint, scan mode, hash rounds, entropy depth, extended signals or canvas probe must change the browser_fp.
